column1: # Recurring English words that are translated, not kept in English letters (style guide sg3).
# `<English>\t<Japanese>[\trequired]` per line. Every entry in this first block is what the human quest corpus
# (counts over trusted human lines whose English has the word). Names never go here: a name stays
# in English letters. A capitalised entry ("Light") is also exempt from translate_lint's
# name_missing check, because it is a translated word, not a name.
# Titles and common nouns used on their own: translated, even when capitalised
# ("the Captain", "His Majesty"). Directly in front of a name they are part of the name and stay in English
# letters ("Captain Althea", "King Magni"); translate_lint checks that. Renderings are chosen, not corpus
# counts. One rendering per term: a Japanese `/` pair fails translate_lint (`slash`).
# More titles used on their own, same rule: "the Mayor of Darkshire" → Darkshireの町長, "Mayor Oakley" stays English.
# A profession trainer keeps the skill name in English, as the
# interface shows it, and translates the role: "Skinning Trainer" → Skinningのトレーナー. "the Arch Druid" alone is
# 大ドルイド; before a name it stays English with the name ("Arch Druid Hamuul").
# More titles and common nouns used on their own. "Commendation
# Officer" is one role, so both words are listed. "the Holy Light" is the faith in quest and gossip text (the
# paladin spell is only in spell tooltips, which are not drafted): 聖なる光. "Bank" in a sentence is 銀行; a bare
# Races and classes are written in katakana in prose, with exactly the spellings
# the addon uses when it fills `{race}` / `{class}` (Core/Placeholders.lua), so a drafted word and a filled
# token read the same. Interface labels (character sheet, "Level 60 Tauren Druid") stay in English.
# `required`: translate_lint fails a draft whose English has the word (or its plural) and whose Japanese lacks it.
# adjective forms of the same words
# is a priest addressed by his title (神父); a lower-case "father" is a parent (父) and is never flagged, so
# only the address is meant here. "the Auction House" in a sentence is オークションハウス (the interface
# writes オークション); a bare "Auction House" label ships as the English. Before a name these all stay in
# English letters with the name, as every other glossary term does.
# A day of the week is not a name: it is translated.
# Ordinary words book headings, letters and plaques capitalise; they recurred
# on 3+ pages in the name review ("Dear Diary,", "Uldaman, Day 4", "The Fate of Carlin Redpath", "State of the
# Cult, Volume 233", "Deathstalker Mission Report", "the Army", "By Blood and Honor We Serve"). Preferred
